decisions.reason: The requirement already monitors the complete 5V rail; identifying the LED load more precisely does not change its monitoring behavior.
The current 3.3V DCDC1 load coverage excludes the LEDs, and the decision to power them from 5V leaves that state unchanged.
The AXP2101 remains the normal source for all system loads regardless of the downstream rail used by the LEDs.
The charge-status interface identifies its SK6812 LED supply as 3.3V, while the client now necessarily requires the SK6812 chain to use 5V.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: The SK6812 minimum supply voltage is 3.5–3.7V so 3.3V is actually below spec, the LED might not light up reliably. Power it from 5V and use the 74AHCT1G125 level shifter (LCSC C151417) on the data line since at 5V the data threshold becomes 3.5V which is above what the ESP32 outputs. That's already in the design, so no changes needed just replace the IRLML2402 with the 74AHCT1G125.

decisions.reason: The LED supply and level-shifter decision does not alter the battery connector or its unresolved pin order.
The decision does not change battery protection circuitry, thresholds, or functions.
The decision does not affect the battery NTC connection or thermal-protection behavior.
The current standalone USB-powered 3.3V load list already excludes the LEDs, so assigning the LEDs to 5V requires no change.
A complete same-message MODIFY already records the 5V supply, required level shifting, and 74AHCT1G125 selection.
The source decision changes the addressable-LED electrical interface, not any sensor-board connector or pinout.
The LED power and data-level decision does not alter native USB routing, enumeration, or programming behavior.
The existing interboard interface already carries the 5V rail and 5V_EN signal; the LED decision does not change its connectors, routes, or pinouts.
